emma: Quick check — I'm preparing a small client change so customers can opt out of telemetry at runtime (disable client metrics + UA header). Before I open the PR: any obvious gotchas with streaming + retries? TL;DR: is it safe to suppress X-Redwood-UA and client metrics on retry or reconnect, or does that break routing/fallbacks?

raj: Short answer: you can suppress UA and the client metrics payload for privacy/reg compliance, but do NOT strip tracing headers (traceparent, tracestate, baggage). We rely on them for correlation and to link retries to original requests. If traces disappear, debugging and observability suffer.

sam: A couple notes from SDK behavior: for streaming (chunked / server-sent events) the JS SDK maintains a small session header for in-flight state — removing it mid-stream will definitely break reconnect semantics. Telemetry toggle is safe if applied at init or per-call. Example for py: 
```
# python SDK (pseudo)
client = RedwoodClient(telemetry_enabled=False)
# or env
export REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=0
```

zoe: Also watch model-selection headers. The server uses an X-Redwood-Model hint and a hashed token_corpus header to pick the right variant and rate-limit buckets. We never include raw prompt/token data, but removing the hashed header can push requests into a more conservative throttle path. So keep model and hashed-corpus headers.

emma: Good catch. Language-specific stuff: in node some fetch wrappers re-add default headers on retry — so UA-suppression must run on each attempt. Any concrete examples?

raj: Right — in node our retry layer clones the original Request and merges defaults back in, so if you set UA to empty on the initial request but don't override the retry logic, the default UA can reappear. Fix: apply a header-normalizer in the retry handler. In python requests, prepared requests copy headers; set on Session or attach a request hook so every attempt is normalized.

devex-bot: Related docs: https://redwood.dev/docs/sdk/telemetry — includes env toggles and per-call override notes. Also: REDWOOD_CLIENT_TELEMETRY=off is supported in 2.1+.

sam: Another practical gotcha: disabling telemetry reduces the sample size for our quality/regression detectors. If a customer disables telemetry globally, their prompts won't be part of sampled evals and we might miss regressions. Recommend offering a per-route or per-call opt-out rather than global for long-lived customers.

zoe: We already have per-call override in v2.1: client.generate(..., telemetry=False). If it's not documented for both py + js, I can add docs and a tiny test matrix. I'll PR that after lunch.

emma: I'll open the PR to: (1) ensure header-normalizer runs in retry path for node+py, (2) expose env var names in README, and (3) add a small integration test that asserts trace headers persist but UA/metrics can be toggled. Pinging @sam @raj for quick review.

raj: Ack, I can review the retry hook changes. If helpful I can spin up a minimal echo server that returns headers so tests can assert correctness.

sam: I can review tests and run them against the current CI job; I have a flaky streaming test though, so happy to pair to stabilize.

devex-bot: deploy-bot: CI queued for branch sdk/telemetry-optout (build #2543).

emma: Thanks all — I'll drop a PR link here once ready and attach the minimal reproducer. :+1:

sam: Nice. One last tweak: call out the exact headers to preserve in the PR description: traceparent, tracestate, baggage, X-Redwood-Model, X-Redwood-Token-Hash. Saves reviewers time.

emma: Will do.

raj: If anyone wants to test a custom harness, DM me and I'll provide an ephemeral endpoint that echoes headers and returns a small chunked stream to emulate reconnects.

zoe: heading to lunch, will open docs PR after.

emma: End of thread for now — thanks!
